reconcile.note: Gill holds Matthew and Levi are the same apostle under two names, using the label by which he was best known.

discrepancy.note: Strauss argues the apostle-lists never call Matthew 'Levi,' so the two-names harmonization has no textual support.

quotes.text: not only do they omit the name of Levi as the earlier or more proper appellation of Matthew, but they leave him undistinguished by the epithet, ὁ τελώνης (the publican), added by the first Evangelist in his catalogue (x. 3); thus proving that they do not consider the Apostle Matthew to be identical with the Levi summoned from the receipt of custom.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, §72 (1846), on Matthew 9:9 and Mark 2:14.

sides.snippet: As Jesus passed by from there, he saw a man called Matthew sitting at the tax collection office. He said to him, \"Follow me.\" He got up and followed him.
sides.verseText: As Jesus passed by from there, he saw a man called Matthew sitting at the tax collection office. He said to him, \"Follow me.\" He got up and followed him.

sides.snippet: As he passed by, he saw Levi, the son of Alphaeus, sitting at the tax office, and he said to him, \"Follow me.\" And he arose and followed him.
